name: France
tagline: The most visited country on earth, and still mostly empty fifty kilometres from anywhere famous.
summary: France is the size of Texas with every landscape Europe offers: Atlantic surf, alpine glacier, Mediterranean cliff, volcanic upland and four hundred kilometres of vineyard between them. It receives more visitors than any country in the world, and almost all of them go to the same six places — which leaves the Auvergne, the Jura, the Aveyron and half of Brittany to whoever bothers. Food and wine are not a sector here; they are the organising principle.

season.note: Paris in October is better than Paris in July: warm enough, half the queue, and the light is famously kinder. The whole country goes on holiday in August and the cities empty while the coast fills. September is harvest in the vineyards, which is the best and busiest time to be in them.

getting_around: The TGV network makes Paris–Marseille three hours and Paris–Bordeaux two. Book on the day fares open and pay a third. Rural France needs a car; the regional TER trains are slow, cheap and lovely if you have the time.
food: Bread bought twice a day, because it is worth nothing by evening
Cheese as a course, in order, before dessert
The regional dish that is not exported: cassoulet, choucroute, aligot, socca — each belongs to one place

festivals.name: Fête de la Musique — free music on every street

know: Lunch is 12 to 2 and a rural kitchen closes at 13:45 regardless of your plans.
Bonjour on entering a shop is not optional politeness; skipping it reads as rudeness.
Many museums are free on the first Sunday of the month, and unbearable on it.

regions.name: Paris & Île-de-France
regions.summary: The capital and the palaces and cathedrals within an hour of it.

cities.name: Paris
cities.summary: Nineteenth-century town planning at monumental scale, with the world's densest concentration of art inside it.
highlights: The Musée d'Orsay in a railway station, better than the Louvre for a single visit
Père Lachaise, a walled city of the dead with its own map
The covered passages of the 2nd, from the 1820s
A market street — rue Mouffetard, rue des Martyrs — early on a Sunday

experiences.name: A market street before ten
experiences.summary: Cheese, bread, a rotisserie chicken and a bottle, then eat it in a park; the most Parisian thing available and it costs almost nothing.

experiences.name: The covered passages
experiences.summary: Glass-roofed arcades built before the department store and mostly forgotten since — a two-hour walk in the dry.

cities.name: Chartres
cities.summary: The most complete Gothic cathedral in France, with 172 windows of 12th-century glass that survived two wars in boxes.
highlights: The blue of the Notre-Dame de la Belle-Verrière window
The labyrinth in the nave floor, walkable on Fridays in summer
The old town below, on the river

regions.name: Normandy & Brittany
regions.summary: Tidal islands, invasion beaches, cider country and a Celtic peninsula that faces the Atlantic.

cities.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
cities.summary: An abbey on a rock in a bay with the fastest tides in Europe, and a village winding up to it.
highlights: The abbey at opening or on a night visit, not at noon
Walking the bay barefoot with a guide, which is the only safe way
The tide, which moves faster than a person walks on spring highs

experiences.name: Cross the bay on foot
experiences.summary: Guided, barefoot, over quicksand and channels; the mount is a different thing entirely when you arrive the medieval way.

cities.name: Bayeux & the Landing Beaches
cities.summary: A town that kept its cathedral, its 70-metre embroidery of 1066, and the beaches of 1944 twenty minutes away.
highlights: The Bayeux Tapestry, seen slowly with the audio guide
Omaha and the American cemetery above it
Arromanches, where the concrete harbour is still in the sea

cities.name: Saint-Malo
cities.summary: A corsair city inside granite ramparts, rebuilt stone by stone after 1944, with a tidal range of twelve metres.
highlights: The ramparts circuit at high tide, when spray comes over
Walking to the Grand Bé island at low water — and watching the clock
Oysters at Cancale, ten kilometres east

regions.name: The Loire & the Southwest
regions.summary: Renaissance châteaux on a wide slow river, then Bordeaux, the dunes and the Basque coast.

cities.name: Amboise & the Loire châteaux
cities.summary: A royal town on the Loire, with Leonardo's last house at the top of it and Chenonceau downstream.
highlights: Chenonceau, built across the river itself
Clos Lucé, where Leonardo died in 1519
Cycling the Loire à Vélo between châteaux, all of it flat

experiences.name: Château to château by bicycle
experiences.summary: 900 km of signed, flat riverside route; two days of it between Blois and Tours is the best introduction.

cities.name: Bordeaux
cities.summary: An 18th-century stone city on a river bend, cleaned in the 2000s, with the world's most famous vineyards at the gates.
highlights: The Place de la Bourse and its mirror of water
Saint-Émilion, a monolithic church cut into rock, forty minutes east
The Cité du Vin, which is better than it sounds

experiences.name: A small Saint-Émilion cellar
experiences.summary: Skip the classified growths and visit a family making 20,000 bottles; you will taste from the barrel and be told the truth about the vintage.

cities.name: Biarritz & the Basque Coast
cities.summary: Atlantic surf, a Napoleonic resort, and a food culture that belongs to a nation without a state.
highlights: Surf at the Côte des Basques, where European surfing started in 1957
Pintxos across the border in San Sebastián, an hour away
Espelette peppers drying on house fronts in September

regions.name: The Alps & the East
regions.summary: Mont Blanc, the Jura, Burgundy's slope of vineyards and Alsace's timbered villages.

cities.name: Chamonix
cities.summary: A valley town under the highest mountain in western Europe, where alpinism was invented.
highlights: Aiguille du Midi by cable car to 3,842 metres, in twenty minutes
The Mer de Glace, and the ladders marking where the ice used to be
The Tour du Mont Blanc, which starts and finishes here

experiences.name: Down to the Mer de Glace
experiences.summary: The steps to the ice are signed with the year the glacier reached each level; the descent is a chronology as much as a walk.

cities.name: Beaune
cities.summary: The wine capital of Burgundy, inside its own walls, on the most valuable agricultural land on earth.
highlights: The Hôtel-Dieu's glazed tile roof and 15th-century wards
Walking or cycling the Côte de Beaune between named vineyards
The Hospices auction in November

cities.name: Colmar & the Alsace wine road
cities.summary: Half-timbered, geranium-hung, and German four times in a century — the food and the wine still say so.
highlights: The Isenheim Altarpiece at the Unterlinden, which stops people mid-sentence
The wine road south through Eguisheim and Riquewihr
Christmas markets, which here are the real thing

regions.name: Provence & the Mediterranean
regions.summary: Roman engineering, lavender, the light the painters came for, and a coast that invented the summer holiday.

cities.name: Arles
cities.summary: A Roman arena still in use, the Rhône delta at the door, and the year Van Gogh painted two hundred canvases here.
highlights: The amphitheatre, built in 90 AD and still hosting events
The Camargue: salt, white horses, flamingos, and a rice crop
Les Rencontres, Europe's oldest photography festival, in July

experiences.name: The Camargue from a horse
experiences.summary: The local white horses are bred to work in water; a half-day gets you into marsh no vehicle reaches.

cities.name: Marseille
cities.summary: France's oldest city, founded by Greeks in 600 BC, Mediterranean rather than French in almost every respect.
highlights: The Calanques: white limestone inlets, reachable on foot from the edge of town
MuCEM and the footbridge to the fort
Bouillabaisse where the fishermen eat, not on the Vieux-Port strip

experiences.name: Walk into the Calanques
experiences.summary: From Luminy to Sugiton in ninety minutes; in summer access is capped and booked, which is why the water is still clear.

cities.name: Nice
cities.summary: An Italian city until 1860, with an old town that still cooks like one and a pebble bay that never closes.
highlights: The Cours Saleya market, and socca eaten standing up
Matisse and Chagall museums up the hill in Cimiez
The train east to Menton along the coast, for the price of a coffee
